title: Victory Vaka joins Middle Tennessee after NCAA fight funded by Lil Wayne - CBS Sports
description: Vaka lost his scholarship at Western Kentucky while grieving his mother's death, but thanks to a legal challenge
body:
Vaka lost his scholarship at Western Kentucky while grieving his mother's death, but thanks to a legal challenge funded by rapper Lil Wayne, he has a new home
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Less than a week after being granted an injunction against the NCAA that prevents it from enforcing its transfer rules, former Western Kentucky defensive tackle Victory Vaka signed with Middle Tennessee on Monday. Vaka filed a lawsuit on Aug. 5 against the NCAA, suing for the ability to transfer after the Hilltoppers non-renewed his scholarship. He entered the portal on Aug. 20 and signed with Middle Tennessee five days later. The Blue Raiders open their season on Sept. 5 against Murray State. Vaka is eligible to play for Middle Tennessee immediately. 
        
            
                Class of 2022 athletes lose NCAA eligibility again with more chaos coming for college football, basketball
                
                    Chris Hummer                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Vaka, a redshirt senior who transferred in from Texas Southern, flew home to California in early April to grieve his mom's death. Vaka told CBS Sports he always planned to return to Western Kentucky for the 2026 season. Nine days before his mom's funeral in May, he received a call from an assistant strength coach. Vaka said the coach provided him with a summer workout plan and told Vaka he was expected back in June.
A few weeks later, on May 27, the Hilltoppers informed Vaka they were canceling his scholarship due to his failure to report with the rest of his team. That designation of a "failure to report" prevented Vaka from entering the transfer portal under the NCAA's aid-and-reduction-or-cancellation exception.Vaka was set to graduate in the fall. He had one remaining year of eligibility remaining. But with no ability to transfer, Vaka was left with no way to play his final season.Vaka's story drew national attention after CBS Sports wrote about it in July.That includes rapper Lil Wayne, who paid for Vaka's legal fees after hearing about his story.
"Fabian Marasciullo, his manager, reached out to me saying the story touched Wayne and he wanted to help in any way possible," Vaka's agent, Jaykwon Jefferson, told CBS Sports. Wayne paid for the costs associated with hiring college sports attorney Darren Heitner and also flew Vaka and his brother out to his concert on Aug. 1 to meet him. Jefferson called the financial assistance "a major lifesaver." The NCAA and Heitner were in talks to settle the case out of court, but that fell apart in recent weeks, leading to Vaka's lawsuit. 
The 6-foot-3, 335-pound DT is a journeyman in college football terms. He's played for four schools and said he hoped Western Kentucky would be his last.Looking back at the situation, Vaka told CBS Sports in July he could have communicated better. Other than Western Kentucky flying Vaka back to campus in mid-April and his call with the strength coach, the two sides had no communication between Vaka's mom's death and the staff asking him to report in late May.Vaka said he told the staff at the time that he thought he could return in June, but offered to return sooner to avoid being removed from the roster.
Western Kentucky did eventually help Vaka file a legislative relief waiver, but that process puts the Hilltoppers in a situation where they basically had to file a waiver against themselves, per CCHA Law partner Paia LaPalombara, because NCAA rules only allow schools to cancel scholarships under limited exceptions."This puts institutions (between) a rock and a hard place -- they may want to support a (student-athlete) getting the additional 30-day window, but doing so also means that they're admitting to their own Level III violation by impermissibly removing the (student-athlete's) aid," LaPalombara said via text."WKU may have actually put forward a good-faith waiver request to the NCAA to allow the (student-athlete) to enter the portal, as they don't want the (student-athlete) to stay at WKU but also can't (or don't want to) admit to a violation that they impermissibly removed the SA's aid."
Vaka's case illustrates one of the gaps in the NCAA's current system.Western Kentucky moved on from him months after the transfer portal closed. By classifying his departure as a disciplinary matter, the school prevented him from using the NCAA's aid-cancellation exception.

title: DeWanna Bonner landing spots: Three WNBA championship contenders who could add star veteran - CBS Sports
description: Bonner is leaving the Mercury with Phoenix out of playoff contention, so where could the 39-year-old land?
body:
Bonner is leaving the Mercury with Phoenix out of playoff contention, so where could the 39-year-old land?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:54 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        WNBA veteran DeWanna Bonner has agreed to a buyout with the Phoenix Mercury, giving the six-time All-Star a chance to compete for a championship in what could potentially be her last season in the league. The question now is where could the 39-year-old finish her accomplished career?Bonner already won two titles in 2009 and 2014, both with Phoenix. Besides four years with Connecticut and part of a season with the Fever, she has mostly been part of the Mercury. In her 17th WNBA season, the 6-foot-4 wing is averaging 10.6 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. She is a versatile, dynamic scorer and an elite rebounder, ranking in the top five for most career rebounds in league history.The timing of the buyout was not by chance. The Mercury (13-24) have officially been eliminated from the playoffs, so this gives her a chance to go out on top if she is planning to retire after this season."Because of the relationship we have with DeWanna, we worked out a buyout agreement that gives her the opportunity to chase a title in what could be her final postseason," said Phoenix General Manager Nick U'ren in an official statement. "DeWanna will always be part of the Mercury family, and we wish her all the best."
Here are the top three landing spots for Bonner:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Las Vegas AcesAfter starting forward NaLyssa Smith suffered a non-contact left knee injury against Toronto on Sunday, Bonner's availability seems like perfect timing. While we don't have an update on the seriousness of Smith's injury yet, there is no doubt Bonner could help the reigning champion Aces during the last stretch of the regular season -- especially since depth has been an issue after the departure of Chennedy Carter.The fit makes a lot of sense, but there is a very big "if." Las Vegas does not currently have the cap space and would need to get a hardship exception. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta DreamThis is another team that needs the depth, as the Dream are averaging the second-fewest bench points per game (17.4) in the league this season, per Statmuse. Bonner is a versatile player with veteran leadership who would give Atlanta more options at the wing. 
The Dream (24-13) sit fourth in the WNBA standings, just one game behind the Aces whom they beat last week. Atlanta is a championship contender, especially with Angel Reese playing some of the best basketball of her career. Also of importance: the Dream do have the cap space to sign Bonner.
        
            
                WNBA Power Rankings: Angel Reese's career week has Dream back in title contention
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Liberty This is a tricky one because although the Liberty (23-15, sixth in the WNBA) looked talented on paper at the beginning of the season, it's questionable whether they are a serious championship contender. Perhaps Bonner could help them turn things around as the postseason approaches. New York does have the cap space, and it makes sense to add depth to the front court while forward Satou Sabally is away indefinitely due to lingering symptoms from a concussion.
Honorable mentionsThe Dallas Wings have cap space and could use reinforcements after losing rookie star Azzi Fudd, who was one of the top defensive pieces for the team. However, they've had some rough stretches recently and are a championship longshot.The Minnesota Lynx are currently the top seed, and Bonner would give them another lengthy wing. But they do not have the cap space

title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from courtside seat at WNBA game after altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud - CBS Sports
description: The former NBA player has requested eligibility for the WNBA Draft amid the row over transgender inclusion in the
body:
The former NBA player has requested eligibility for the WNBA Draft amid the row over transgender inclusion in the league
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CHICAGO -- Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from his courtside seat during the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky on Sunday after getting into a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Late in the third quarter, Cloud drove to the basket and converted a tough finish that drew a timeout from Fever coach Stephanie White. As players from both teams went to their respective benches, Cloud began pointing and yelling at Kanter Freedom, who stood up and walked toward the court. An official and security personnel immediately jumped in, and Cloud's teammates arrived to pull her away from the situation. The official gestured for Kanter Freedom to be ejected and both team and arena security escorted him away from his seat. He tried to protest in an area behind the courtside seating for a short period before eventually leaving to a chorus of boos and middle fingers.Kanter Freedom -- who was wearing a black t-shirt that read "woman noun adult human female" -- has used social media to become part of the conversation around transgender athletes.

                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            In the wake of Fever guard Sophie Cunningham's comments about transgender athletes, Kanter Freedom has spent the past few weeks agitating to be eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft, along with fellow former NBA player Royce White. Both Kanter Freedom and White have claimed that they now identify as women. Kanter Freedom spent 11 years playing in the NBA, most recently for the Celtics in the 2021-22 season. The Türkiye native added Freedom to his name when he became an American citizen in 2021. CBS Sports spoke to sources around the league who said they do not think the eligibility of Kanter Freedom and White is a legitimate matter and view their recent actions as publicity stunts.Cloud and Sky coach reactCloud did not speak with the media after Sunday's game. She did meet with team and league security. She later made a statement on social media. 
"To every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You're loved. You're seen. You're perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me," Cloud wrote. 
"I talked to the team and Tash didn't want to feel like she was a distraction. I told her she wasn't," Sky coach Tyler Marsh said in his post-game press conference. "I told her we all embrace her as someone who protects our team and people who need to be protected. Tash is always gonna stand on that and we stand for Tash.""There's so many good things about this league and so many good things about the play of these players, that if you come to a game, you should probably come to enjoy the basketball," Marsh added. "That seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too."
Fever star Caitlin Clark said that she did not see the incident, and both she and Lexie Hull shook their heads no when asked if Kanter Freedom had said anything to them during the game. Fever coach Stephanie White said that it is "important that people like you guys in this room don't give it any gas. It's a social media thing."This is not the first time that Cloud and Kanter Freedom have crossed paths. In 2023, the two went back and forth on social media after Cloud criticized the United States government.  WNBA has called out 'bad-faith efforts'The WNBA has become a battleground for the debate about transgender athletes over the last month after Cunningham said in an ESPN profile that she wants to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men." 
Later, Cunningham doubled down prior to the Fever's win over the Connecticut Sun on July 22. "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense," she said. "And I think I'll always believe in that. I think it's really important to protect children, and that's little girls who are also involved in that category. I stand on what I said."Cunningham added that she doesn't "dislike anyone" and that there's "room to love everyone." She continued, "I'm also there to love biological women, and I think that there are rights that need to be protected. And, like I said, I'm gonna stand true to that. I'll never falter in my beliefs in that. But I have never once stated that I hated the trans community."The WNBA has never had a transgender player and does not have a public policy about transgender participation. The new collective bargaining agreement states simply that, "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." 
Earlier this month, the WNBA convened a task force to discuss the issue and made a statement that read, in part, "We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."

title: Marshall Manning recruiting: Peyton Manning's son makes high school debut - CBS Sports
description: Although 15-year-old freshman Marshall Manning played only two snaps in his varsity debut, Baylor coach Erik Kimr
body:
Although 15-year-old freshman Marshall Manning played only two snaps in his varsity debut, Baylor coach Erik Kimrey plans to get Peyton Manning's son game action every week to prepare him for the future.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It was only two snaps, but for Marshall Manning, it was the first real entry on what figures to be a very long recruiting résumé. The 15-year-old freshman quarterback and son of Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning made his high school debut Thursday night as Chattanooga (Tennessee) Baylor School defeated Brentwood (Tennessee) Academy 38-20 in a nationally televised game.Manning entered in the second quarter and immediately completed an 8-yard pass to Antwaun "Cornbread" Adams -- a four-star safety in the 2028 class -- for a first down.He handed the ball off on his next snap and returned to the sideline. Sadly there were no "Omaha!" audibles or line of scrimmage finger licks, but Manning did don the No. 16 his dad wore at Tennessee. 
The two players weren't nearly enough to draw any conclusions about Manning as a prospect. His coach, Erik Kimrey, has a bigger plan for him.
"I want Marshall to play in every game this year, even if it's just two plays like that," Kimrey said. "Hopefully, it'll be a lot more, but I felt like -- we need him next year, and he needs to get ready."Even if his recruiting process is still years away from becoming serious, Manning's presence on a varsity field is going to draw attention simply because of who he is and who came before him.Marshall is the grandson of Archie Manning, the son of Peyton Manning, the nephew of Eli Manning and the cousin of Texas quarterback Arch Manning. Like Arch, he will have to navigate the reality that his last name makes him a national recruiting story long before he has had a chance to establish himself as a prospect.
Manning is part of the 2030 class, meaning he won't be eligible to sign with a college until December 2029. That's still some 1,200 days away. He will have opportunities throughout his freshman season to build a body of work. And given his last name, there will be no shortage of people watching."I believe we are going to see a lot of Marshall Manning this fall," 247Sports recruiting analyst Tom Loy said. "I expect him to get plenty of opportunities on the field to show what he can do."
Has Marshall Manning begun his recruiting process?Loy described Manning as a confident, intelligent player who can handle the moment when called upon, while noting that his physical development will be important as he gets older (Marshall is listed at 5-foot-11). "As he continues to see the field, it'll give everyone an opportunity to truly evaluate him, both from a scouting perspective and when it comes to potential scholarship offers," Loy said.Baylor is already looking toward Manning as a potential answer at quarterback in the future. Every additional snap will give college coaches more to evaluate, from his arm talent and decision-making to his athleticism and physical development.
There will inevitably be speculation about where Manning could eventually play. Tennessee and Ole Miss are obvious names given the Manning family's ties to both programs, but Loy cautioned against trying to project a recruitment that is only beginning."This is a new era of college football and high school recruiting," Loy said. "It is all about fit. This is a prospect with a long way to go in his process, as things are just beginning for the freshman. All that said, as long as he continues to grow and fill out physically, the big boys of the SEC are surely going to come calling."Thursday night was only two snaps. But for the next Manning quarterback, the evaluation has officially begun.

title: Three Fantasy Football sleepers Jacob Gibbs can't stop drafting - CBS Sports
description: Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his rost
body:
Jacob Gibbs is moving these sleepers up his draft boards and leaving his late-August drafts with them on his roster
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        I wrote up Jonathon Brooks in this morning's newsletter. Here's a link, if you missed that. My favorite sleepers this off-season have been Brooks, Josh Downs, and Jayden Reed. Brooks is no longer a sleeper. Downs and Reed still are! I write about them all of the time, though. You can read about those two here. So let's transition to three players the Fantasy Football community and more importantly your home league drafts are still probably sleeping on!Sleeper #1 - Jaylin Noel, WR, Houston TexansJaylin Noel was a very good prospect. In my opinion, he was one of the biggest steals of the 2025 NFL Draft. The Texans landed him in Round 4.His game translated right away as a rookie. He was a great returner. Noel also won down the field, and he won as a pre-snap motion threat on out-breaking routes. He is great tracking the ball, has reliable hands, and is a springy athlete who can create separation.According to Matt Harmon's Reception Perception charting, Noel fell in exclusive company in terms of grading out 70th percentile or better vs. man, press, and zone coverage in 2025. He's free in drafts. The Texans traded for Kayshon Boutte, but a late-August add leads to a ramp-up period to learn the scheme and get on the same page as C.J. Stroud in the passing game. 
Sleeper #2 - Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver BroncosDenver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman is not free in drafts, but I do believe he is underrated. He's the Denver Broncos RB who I have ranked the highest. The opening schedule for the Broncos is pretty rough. The second half of the season looks nice, on paper.I expect Coleman to play a role on passing downs (and potentially in short-yardage situations) right away for the Broncos. I was extremely impressed with his college film, particularly in pass protection. The Broncos felt the same way. Sean Payton said, "That was a strong suit when you were looking at his tape -- different than the rest of the class," in reference to Coleman's pass protection.If there's an injury in the backfield, Coleman has a three-down skill set. He's ready to step into a bell-cow role in a top-half-of-the-league offense. And I really do think there's a lot to like about his tape as a runner. His rushing efficiency was up-and-down in college, and many view him as a plodder because he's a little buff boi. There were flashes of tempo, block-setting, and decent burst early in the 2025 season from Coleman, before he got banged-up and his offensive line struggled to close out the season. If he's a better rusher than many expect, Coleman might not need an injury to carve out a Fantasy-friendly role for himself in this backfield.
He's a bit more expensive than some of my favorite upside bench stashes -- Demond Claiborne, Emmett Johnson, Kaelon Black, and Adam Randall -- but I do view Coleman as worth a Round 10 draft pick if in need of bench RB upside.Sleeper #3 - Cyrus Allen, WR, Kansas City ChiefsI'm buying the Cyrus Allen hype. Why wouldn't we? He was productive in college, and his film backed it up. The ways he won feel sustainable. It wasn't schemed-up college nonsense. It wasn't picking on poor competition. He was winning routes. He was winning at the catch point. He has a good feel for space and was consistently presenting an open target vs. zone coverage.The drumbeat coming out of Chiefs training camp has been loud and consistent. Allen looked great in the first preseason game. Everything points towards this being a talented player who was overlooked in the NFL Draft. It happens every year.
Allen feels a bit buried on the depth chart (no surprise, we're talking about a rookie WR in August), but let's not pretend as if this Chiefs receiver room has any stalwarts on it. This is as inconsistent of a WR room as we are going to find in the NFL (Dolphins always excluded from this type of discussion). Any or all three of the Chiefs top receivers could miss time. Or Allen could just prove to be the best one. Check out the Rashee Rice Reception Perception profile. The Chiefs don't have a consistent separator. Or, they have not had one. Maybe they do now!

title: Why De'Von Achane remains a top-15 pick in Fantasy Football rankings - CBS Sports
description: Regression feels inevitable for the talented Dolphins running back, but that doesn't mean you should forget about
body:
Regression feels inevitable for the talented Dolphins running back, but that doesn't mean you should forget about him at the top of Fantasy Football drafts
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- The first two times Malik Willis was pressured against a very fast New York pass rush resulted in two hurried throws, neither of which were in the area code of his running back.It was exactly what prospective Fantasy managers of De'Von Achane feared. Willis is known for his mobility, arm strength, and lack of targets to his running backs, in that order. Over the past two years, only Anthony Richardson threw at a lower rate to his running backs than Willis at 10.2%.But as a quality quarterback should, Willis adjusted. Over the rest of his 11-on-11 snaps in the Dolphins' joint practice against the Giants, Willis frequently targeted Achane. By my count, Achane had three designed targets, including one in the end zone called back by a penalty on top of two checkdowns when Willis was under duress.It's not nothing. This was evidence that the Dolphins under offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik were able to adjust in real time to an opponent and make good use of their most effective offensive weapon.
It is a good sign for Achane to retain a lot more of his Fantasy value from 2025 than initially anticipated. Just don't expect a full repeat of his monster season.Of Achane's 1,838 total yards and 12 total touchdowns, 488 yards and four scores came over 67 of the 85 targets he caught. In a full PPR league, those receiving totals accounted for 43 percent of his PPR total points. That came in a year where Tua Tagovailoa was his primary thrower and Mike McDaniel was his playcaller. There seemed to be an emphasis on Tagovailoa getting the ball out quickly, and frequently it went to Achane (Tagovailoa had a 26.3% target rate to his running backs since 2024).It is believed that the Dolphins will move into a version of the West Coast offense similar to what Willis ran in Green Bay. Its limitations may only be rooted in whatever it is Willis is unable to effectively do. Given what we saw from him with the Packers, that might not be a long list, which is great for the Dolphins.
Plus it doesn't hurt that Achane had the equivalent of a long touchdown run in team drills against the Giants thanks to some excellent blocking from the right side of his offensive line. He appears to be healthy and ready to roll.Other concerns exist surrounding Achane. The Miami offense, for one, is expected to not put up a lot of points. But they ranked 25th in the league in points scored last year (20.4 per game) while running the ball more than the league average (45.5% of the time), and Achane was amazing. It wouldn't be surprising in the least to see the Dolphins match both of those averages this year.And even though coach Jeff Hafley joked about giving Achane "40 to 45" touches a game, the unspoken truth in his statement is that Achane will be leaned on heavily. Such was the case last season when he averaged 14.9 carries and 4.2 catches per game, and he played until Week 18. He's done this before.

        
            
                Why De'Von Achane could chase an NFL record that's stood since 1984: Dolphins coach hints at huge year for RB
                
                    John Breech                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
If Achane routinely gets around 14 carries per game and picks up three catches per game (he averaged just over four last year -- it's a good idea to expect a decrease this year), that's still plenty of good work. Again, it's not nothing.Expecting 20-plus PPR points per game again this year from Achane might be a bit much. But if the receptions will be there to some decent degree, and if the Dolphins offense can at least be as solid as they were last season, then it's not crazy to expect just a small decline in production. Not a big one. Eighteen PPR points per game is on the table, and not a lot of running backs offer that kind of upside. By comparison, Achane has a better outlook in PPR leagues than Omarion Hampton, Saquon Barkley and Derrick Henry.It's why Achane being worth taking as a top-15 pick in full PPR with a drop into Round 2 in half- and non-PPR scoring leagues.

        With less than a minute to play on Saturday night, Angel Reese stepped to the line and knocked down a pair of free throws to seal the Atlanta Dream's 99-89 win over the Phoenix Mercury. The free throws gave Reese a new career-high of 31 points and the first 30-point game of her career, and the win, the Dream's third in a row, officially clinched their spot in the playoffs. After making headlines for missing a potential game-winner against the Indiana Fever last Sunday, Reese responded with one of the best weeks of her career. In the first three games of the Dream's West Coast road trip, Reese is averaging 24 points, 11.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 3.7 steals on 67.4% shooting. The Dream are 3-0 in those games, including a huge win over the Aces, and have moved back into fourth place ahead of the Indiana Fever. 
One game before her career-high night in Phoenix, Reese put up 20 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists on a perfect 9 of 9 from the field to join Nneka Ogwumike and Tamika Williams-Jeter as the only players in WNBA history to shoot 100% from the field in a 20-point, 10-rebound outing. Reese has continued to face criticism this season for her poor efficiency around the basket, and rightfully so. (She's shooting 52.5% in the restricted area on a league-high 337 attempts. Among the 15 players with at least 150 attempts, no one else is shooting below 60%.) But she is the best rebounder in the world and has made such significant strides as a defender that when she is making her shots, as she did this week, she's a top-10 player in the league. 
The Dream are 9-2 when Reese shoots 50% or better this season and 15-11 when she's below that mark. Ahead of her first postseason, the big question for Reese and the Dream is whether she can maintain this recent efficiency. If she can, no one will want to play Atlanta come playoff time.

She also made a key defensive stop on Caitlin Clark late in that contest, showing that her value is about far more than shooting. The Liberty, who still have a chance to earn a top-four seed, are now 11-4 with Fiebich in the lineup this season.

They did end their grueling five-game road trip with a big win over the Sky, however, as Caitlin Clark hit a career-high eight 3s and recorded her fifth career 30-point, 10-assist game, which is more than every other player in WNBA history combined. Awak Kuier, who had a franchise-record seven blocks against Indiana, has been particularly impressive defensively.

However, they would need to win out and would need the Wings to lose out. That's not happening. title: Serie A hot takes: AC Milan's gem shines and could mean less minutes for Pulisic - CBS Sports
description: The first weekend of Serie A action is already in the books and we had some surprises
body:
The first weekend of Serie A action is already in the books and we had some surprises
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026-2027 Serie A season is finally back, and after the first weekend of action, it's already time to reflect on what happened and especially what we can expect ahead of the second matchday that will take place later this week. Inter won convincingly on Saturday, as the 2025–2026 Serie A champions cruised to a dominant 4–1 victory over Monza. Their title rivals responded on Sunday, with AC Milan beating Torino 2–1 and Juventus securing a narrow 1–0 win away at Frosinone, while Napoli won 2-0 at Genoa. Now, time for some hot takes:AC Milan gem takes advantage, but what about Pulisic?The biggest surprise of the first weekend of Serie A action was AC Milan wonderkid Alphadjo Cisse, who scored the opening goal of the 2-1 win against Torino on Sunday. The Italian winger, who will turn 20 in October, is highly valued by his coach Ruben Amorim, who praised him ahead of the match. "I'm in love with him," he said.The Portuguese coach, who replaced Massimiliano Allegri on the bench of the Italian giants this summer, handed Cisse his first Serie A start in his first official league match in charge. Rafael Leao is currently sidelined with an injury and is expected to leave the Rossoneri before transfer deadline day, while American Christian Pulisic is still working his way back to full fitness. It's an opportunity for Cisse to take full advantage and cement himself as the starter on the left wing. Cisse proved to be at the level asked by Amorim, and he's expected to start again on Friday when AC Milan will host Venezia. Leao and Pulisic can wait, it's now time for Cisse to shine. 
As for the American, who suffered a microfracture in his leg in the USMNT's last game at the World Cup, a 4-1 loss to Belgium, his versatility means he should see the field plenty, but a lot will depend on how Amorim evolves at the club. But Cisse's surge isn't great news for Leao, but it shouldn't impact Pulisic all that much when he's healthy.
Andy Diouf: Inter unexpected starInter started off well their debut Serie A game of the season as the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners won 4-1 against Monza at San Siro on Saturday. Hakan Calhanoglu, Francesco Pio Esposito, Yann Bisseck and Piotr Zielinski all scored in the opening game but the MVP of the match was Andy Diouf, the French winger who delivered two key assists against Monza.His performances are great news for Nerazzurri coach Cristian Chivu, who decided to deploy him as a right wing-back in Inter's 3-5-2 system last season, despite the player arriving from Lens in the summer of 2025 as a central midfielder. Last year, when Denzel Dumfries was injured, Chivu tried him in that position and improved drastically in the second part of the season, despite having said multiple times that he was not particularly keen on playing on the right wing. When the Nerazzurri sold Dumfries to Real Madrid this summer, Inter decided to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham but consider Diouf a potential starter in that position as well. In the end, Chivu was not wrong. 
The mistake of Spalletti After winning 1-0 in the opening game against Frosinone, Juventus coach Luciano Spalletti spoke about the Bianconeri striker Randal Kolo Muani, who didn't score in his Serie A debut after arriving from PSG in the summer. Spalletti, speaking to DAZN, didn't really have nice words about the French player and said, "We went and got Kolo, we've looked after him and we know what his value is. But he has to realize that he hasn't played for two years and there must be a reason for that. Sometimes you think you're at an exceptional level but you've left something behind that you need to go and get back."
It's a risky choice from Spalletti to speak about one of his best players in this way. Kolo Muani is now a key striker for Juventus after the Italian club decided to not sign a new deal with former striker Dusan Vlahovic, who ended up signing with Besiktas later in the summer transfer window. Spalletti is not new to making strong statements about his players, but comments like these could easily backfire, particularly when aimed at a player who has quickly become an important part of the team ahead of the upcoming season.

title: 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio, pleads no contest - CBS Sports
description: York was sentenced to two days in jail and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines
body:
York was sentenced to two days in jail and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO Jed York was arrested in East Palestine, Ohio, this weekend and pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, per WKBN. York was sentenced to two days in the Columbiana County Jail with credit for one day served and ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. Court documents obtained by KRON4 state the disorderly conduct charge was amended from engaging in prostitution. York was arrested by the local police department, which was assisting the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, at Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community off state Route 170.
The 49ers released a statement on York's arrest, via ESPN, saying: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."York was born and raised in Youngstown, not far from where he was arrested. He became CEO of the 49ers in 2008 while his parents, John and Denise York, assumed roles of co-chairmen. York's grandfather, Edward DeBartolo Sr., bought the franchise in 1977, while York's uncle, Eddie DeBartolo Jr., served as the team's owner from 1977 to 2000. 
York could be subject to discipline from the league under the personal conduct policy. According to the 49ers' official website, York currently serves on three NFL committees: Stadium, Media O&O (NFL's owned media businesses), Business Ventures, and Fan Engagement and Major Events.

body:
The Tar Heels enter a new era with Michael Malone at the helm of the storied program

        North Carolina will enter a new era this season as Michael Malone takes over the program after a lengthy coaching career in the NBA. The former coach of the Sacramento Kings and Denver Nuggets hasn't coached at the college level in over 25 years, with his last stint coming as an assistant coach at Manhattan before making the jump to the NBA in 2001.Following a loss to VCU in the NCAA Tournament, UNC underwent nearly a two-week-long coaching search and landed on Malone despite his lack of ties to the Carolina program, which was an unofficial prerequisite for several coaches who came before him.North Carolina has the No. 8-ranked transfer portal class in the 247Sports rankings, headlined by the additions of Matt Able (NC State), Terrence Brown (Utah) and Neoklis Avdalas (Virginia Tech). The Tar Heels also welcome five-star big man Sayon Keita from Spain, who is a potential name to know for the 2027 NBA Draft.This roster will look drastically different from last season's, which featured star forward Caleb Wilson, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. The Tar Heels also lost big man Henri Veesaar to the NBA and defensive ace Seth Trimble, who is set to play for Louisville this season if he is granted an extra year of eligibility.
Let's dive into UNC's roster, starting with who might be in the lineup on opening night against Western Carolina on Nov. 2.North Carolina's projected starting lineupG: Terrence Brown | 6-3 | 180 | Sr.The Utah transfer is coming off a season in which he averaged 19.9 points, 3.8 assists and 2.4 rebounds in his first year playing high-major basketball. Brown began his career at Farleigh Dickinson, where he averaged 20.6 points during the 2024-25 campaign. He will bring scoring, playmaking and much-needed athleticism to UNC's lineup.G: Matt Able | 6-5 | 200 | So.Able is the rare Tobacco Road transfer. Able played last season at NC State and averaged 8.8 points and 3.4 rebounds in just over 21 minutes per game. After appearing in 34 games off the bench for the Wolfpack, Able is set to step into a starting role this season with the Tar Heels. He might be UNC's best NBA prospect and could crack the first round with a breakout season.
G: Neoklis Avdalas | 6-9 | 220 | Fr.The 6-foot-9 guard has the archetype of a point-forward that can be extremely valuable at both the college and NBA levels. As a freshman at Virginia Tech, he averaged 12.1 points, 4.6 assists and 3.1 rebounds in 31 games. There were certainly flashes (see the game against Providence in nonconference play) last season that showed Avdalas can be an impact player.F: Jarin Stevenson | 6-10 | 220 | Sr.Stevenson is one of the lone returners on this roster. The former Alabama forward transferred to UNC ahead of last season and started 25 games for the Tar Heels, averaging 8.1 points and 4.4 rebounds. Stevenson played a key role on Alabama's Final Four team as a reserve in 2024 and should slot into the lineup as the starting power forward.C: Cameron Fens | 7-0 | 255 | Sr.The starting center position could be up for grabs heading into the season, with the top candidates being Fens and Keita. Fens, who was granted an extra year of eligibility via a court ruling in Tennessee, was a late addition to UNC's roster. The former South Dakota big man averaged 14.4 points and 8.7 rebounds per game last season. The burly big man brings experience and heft, which UNC needs, but Keita may be the better long-term option here for the Tar Heels.
Off the benchF: Maximo Adams | 6-7 | 205 | Fr.Adams, the No. 31-ranked playerhttps://247sports.com/player/maximo-adams-46136627/in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, stayed true to his pledge despite the coaching change. Adams committed to UNC in November over Texas, Kansas, Michigan State, and Kentucky, among others and signed shortly after. As his 247Sports scouting report notes, he is an "exceptional" mid-range shooter off the dribble.F: Cade Bennerman | 7-0 | 195 | So.Bennerman redshirted during the 2025-26 season at Northwestern and transferred to UNC this offseason. Bennerman was a three-star-rated transfer in the 247Sports rankings and should provide frontcourt depth.C: Sayon Keita | 7-1 | 205 | Fr.Keita has the most NBA upside of anybody on this roster. The projected first-round pick is an athletic 7-footer who can run the floor and protect the rim. Keita should be either UNC's starting center or one of the first players off the bench.
G: Isaiah Denis | 6-4 | 185 | So.Denis appeared in 10 games last season for UNC and could see his role expand with a new-look roster. The former four-star prospect from the 2025 recruiting cycle was the top-ranked player from North Carolina coming out of high school.G: Angelo Brizzi | 6-3 | 200 | Sr.North Carolina will mark Brizzi's fifth school in five years after previous stops at Villanova, Davidson, Longwood and Buffalo. He is coming off the best statistical season of his career after averaging 14.5 points while shooting 37% from the 3-point line this past year at Buffalo.Filling out the rosterF: Jaydon Young | 6-4 | Sr.F: Kevin Thomas | 6-6 | Fr.F: Alexandros Samodurov | 6-11 | Fr.Market watchOdds to win 2027 NCAA Tournament (via FanDuel Sportsbook): +7500 (tied for 32nd-best odds with Villanova)
Vegas is lower on North Carolina heading into this season. However, that projection makes sense because UNC will be ranked in the 20s, or just outside the bubble in the preseason AP Top 25 poll this fall. The Tar Heels have a deeper roster than last season, but they also don't have a blue-chip talent like Wilson. UNC's ceiling will come down to Able and Avdalas taking a Year 2 jump, how good Keita is as a freshman and how quickly Malone adapts to being a college coach.The Tar Heels have a handful of intriguing nonconference games that will be a good measuring stick heading into ACC play. The first test will be on Dec. 1 when UNC hosts Arkansas in the ACC/SEC Challenge. Other games to track include Georgia (Nov. 13), West Virginia (Nov. 27), Butler (Dec. 6), Georgetown (Dec. 12), NC State (Dec. 15), Kentucky (Dec. 19) and Illinois (Jan. 30, 2027).North Carolina will likely be picked to finish fifth in the ACC preseason poll behind Duke, Louisville, Virginia and Miami. The Tar Heels certainly have the talent to be an NCAA Tournament team and make noise in the ACC, but it will come down to those three factors listed in the first paragraph to determine how far UNC can go in March during Malone's first season at the helm.

title: Jamey's do not draft list: 12 players to avoid in Fantasy Football - CBS Sports
description: It's not always easy to admit when you're wrong. In doing this job, I've been wrong a lot -- and you've let me know about it, which is f
body:
It's not always easy to admit when you're wrong. In doing this job, I've been wrong a lot -- and you've let me know about it, which is fair. I should be held accountable for my mistakes.So far, I've done two versions of bust lists for this season. The first one was in early May  and the second one was in late July.Things have changed for several players on those two lists, and my outlook for them has changed as well. It could be injuries to teammates or just a better Average Draft Position.But these players should no longer be considered busts in 2026:Leaving the busts list Travis EtienneMy initial fear was he would be sharing touches with Alvin Kamara, and Kellen Moore doesn't have a great track record throwing to his running backs. The work in the passing game could still be a problem for Etienne, but Kamara suffered a sprained MCL on Aug. 18 and could miss the start of the season -- if not longer. Etienne should be headed for a hefty workload, and Kamara might not be much of a factor for the first half of the season. Etienne's CBS Sports ADP is at 40.4, and that might be too low. You can argue he's a Round 3 pick now that Kamara is injured.
Malik NabersI was concerned Nabers might not be ready for Week 1 coming off last year's torn ACL and meniscus tear in his right knee, but he appears on track for the start of the season. Heading into the third week of the preseason, Nabers has yet to take part in team drills, but that is expected to happen soon. As long as he doesn't suffer a setback, Nabers is worth drafting in Round 3 as a high-end No. 2 Fantasy receiver. I can't sign off on him being a No. 1 Fantasy option, but I'm thrilled to see him make a full recovery. His CBS Sports ADP is just right at 33.3.Tetairoa McMillanI still don't like it when I see McMillan get drafted in Round 3, but his CBS Sports ADP is at 44.3, which is hard to argue with. The reports of him getting more time in the slot in the preseason have been accurate, and that's a big boost to his Fantasy value. Bryce Young is still not the ideal quarterback to help elevate McMillan's production, but he's a great No. 2 Fantasy receiver worth drafting in Round 4. And if the offensive line can get healthy sooner rather than later -- left tackle Iken Ekwonu (knee) and right tackle Taylor Moton (blood clots) are battling injuries -- then this offense could be a nice surprise. Davante AdamsAdams, 33, isn't getting younger, and it was troubling to see him catch just 60 passes for 789 yards last season on 114 targets in 14 games. But we all know he scored 14 touchdowns last year, and he caught at least 11 touchdowns in four of the past six seasons with Green Bay, Las Vegas and the Rams. The reason Adams is no longer a bust is that Puka Nacua (groin) is injured, and he could be facing a suspension, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Nacua is under investigation by the NFL since he is part of a civil case in which he is alleged to have bitten a woman on the shoulder while intoxicated and then made an unprovoked antisemitic remark. Any missed time for Nacua is a boost for Adams, who has a solid CBS Sports ADP of 57.7.
Jameson WilliamsSam LaPorta (hip) was diagnosed with a hip injury on Aug. 20, which is the main reason Williams is no longer a bust. I'm hopeful LaPorta is ready for Week 1, but any absence for him is a huge plus for Williams. In 2025, in nine games with LaPorta, Williams averaged just 10.9 PPR points and 4.8 targets per game. In eight games without LaPorta after he suffered a back injury, Williams averaged 15.2 PPR points and 7.4 targets per game. I still don't love Williams at his CBS Sports ADP of 57.7, but he's worth the risk now in that range if LaPorta could miss any time in the regular season. Chris OlaveI put Olave on the first bust list in May after the Saints drafted Jordyn Tyson in Round 1 of the NFL Draft. Last year, when Rashid Shaheed was in New Orleans, Olave averaged just 14.1 PPR points per game in the first nine outings of the season. But in the final seven games after Shaheed was traded to Seattle, Olave averaged 20.2 PPR points per game. Tyson is dealing with a hamstring injury as of Aug. 14, and he could miss the first half of the season. That puts Olave back in line to be a monster, and he's worth drafting toward the end of Round 2. I love his current CBS Sports ADP of 29.8, but that should rise over the next two weeks.Jaylen WaddleWaddle was on the first bust list in May right after he joined the Broncos, and I was worried that Fantasy managers would draft him too soon. But his CBS Sports ADP is actually low at 51.6, and I would draft him in Round 4. It was a little concerning when he dealt with a leg injury for over a week in August, but it was never considered serious. He has looked good in his return to practice, and he should be the No. 1 receiver for Bo Nix. Hopefully, the Waddle we saw early in his tenure in Miami -- he averaged at least 14.2 PPR points per game in each of the first three seasons of his career -- will show up again in Denver this year.
Now, here are the players that I don't plan to draft in 2026 at their current CBS Sports ADP as of Aug. 24. I will draft them if they fall because these are great players, but I don't expect that to happen.BustsPatrick MahomesMahomes is being drafted as a borderline starter at QB13 with a CBS Sports ADP of 99.3, but I would still pass on him there. He's coming off last year's torn ACL and LCL in his knee, which he suffered in Week 15, and the good news is he'll be ready for Week 1. But I don't expect him to run much, and that's what made him a standout Fantasy quarterback in 2025 at 23.6 points per game. He set a career high for rushing yards (422) and rushing touchdowns (five) in just 14 games, and the Chiefs will likely be cautious with his mobility. Keep in mind that in 2023 and 2024 he averaged less than 21.0 Fantasy points per game, and Kansas City just upgraded its run game with the addition of Kenneth Walker III. Mahomes should be good, he just likely won't be great.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Jaxson Dart (ADP of 106.4), Jared Goff (ADP of 109.5) and Bo Nix (ADP of 117.9)
Christian McCaffreyI have McCaffrey ranked as a first-round pick, but the earliest I would draft him is No. 10 overall. However, his CBS Sports ADP is 7.6. I'm glad he returned to practice Sunday after being out for two weeks due to "tightness," which apparently was a planned absence. But I still have concerns about his outlook. He turned 30 in June and just had 450 total touches in 2025, including the playoffs (337 carries and 113 catches). This is the third time in McCaffrey's career that he had at least 400 total touches in a season (2023 with the 49ers and 2019 with Carolina) and he missed 13 games due to injury the following year both times. We all remember 2024 when he struggled with Achilles and knee problems and was limited to four games. In 2020 in Carolina, McCaffrey played just three games due to three separate injuries (a right high-ankle sprain, a shoulder A/C joint sprain and a thigh/glute strain). We can't predict injuries, but the history suggests McCaffrey might not hold up in 2026. When healthy, he's awesome, and he was just the No. 1 non-quarterback in 2025 at 24.5 PPR points per game. You could be missing the best player in Fantasy if you pass on him. But you also could have a major problem if he gets hurt again after his hefty workload in 2025.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ADP of 9.2), James Cook (ADP of 10.5) and Chase Brown (ADP of 12.5)De'Von AchaneIt appears like Achane is going to get a hefty workload this season based on his preseason appearances. But I'm still not drafting him at his CBS Sports ADP of 11.6, and the earliest I would draft him is No. 15 overall. According to Fantasy Points, the quarterback with the second-highest target rate to running backs since 2023 was Tua Tagovailoa at 24.5 percent (Shedeur Sanders was No. 1 at 25.5 percent). The quarterback with the lowest target rate to running backs over that span was Malik Willis at 10.8 percent. That's telling given how much Achane was involved as a receiver for the Dolphins, as he's averaged 86 targets and 72.5 receptions the past two seasons. Now, Willis will obviously use Achane as a weapon in the passing game, especially given the state of Miami's receiving corps going into the season. But Willis will run much more than Tagovailoa, so expect Achane's production as a receiver to decline this year. We'll also see just how much Tagovailoa's absence -- as well as coach Mike McDaniel -- will hinder Achane. He averaged 21.5 PPR points in 25 games with Tagovailoa in the past two seasons and just 10.5 PPR points in eight games without Tagovailoa over that span. The Dolphins aren't expected to win many games in 2025 -- their projected win total is 4.5 -- so touchdown opportunities could be tough for Achane. I'll let someone else draft Achane in Round 1.
(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Chase Brown (ADP of 12.5), Kenneth Walker III (ADP of 18.7) and Omarion Hampton (ADP of 20.5)Ashton JeantyThis is a tricky one because we don't know where his ADP will end up following his injury scare Sunday afternoon. Thankfully, it's an ankle sprain, but we don't know the severity yet. I'm anticipating a potential absence for Week 1, and we'll see how long this injury lingers. His ADP is 13.7, but the earliest I would draft Jeanty is now Round 3. That might seem like an overreaction, but he already has to overcome being on a bad team -- the Raiders' projected win total is 5.5 -- while Las Vegas has a difficult schedule. I was willing to overlook these concerns given Jeanty's talent, but this injury is now reason to pass on him in the first two rounds. And Mike Washington Jr. could earn a bigger role than expected if he plays well while Jeanty is out.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Saquon Barkley (ADP of 14.1), Kenneth Walker III (ADP of 18.7) and Omarion Hampton (ADP of 20.5)
Jeremiyah LoveLove suffered a high-ankle sprain in Arizona's first preseason game, and he went from a potential Round 2 selection to Round 3 now with an ADP of 32.6. I'm not drafting Love until Round 4, which might be an overreaction, but there's enough risk to pass on him at his current cost. We don't know how long he's going to be out, but you should anticipate him missing Week 1 and being limited early in the season. He's going to share touches with Tyler Allgeier and potentially James Conner, especially with Allgeier likely to vulture touchdown opportunities. The Cardinals also have a brutal schedule, and they aren't expected to win many games with a projected total of 4.5. The offensive line is also worse after second-round pick Chase Bisontis (knee) suffered a torn MCL in the same game Love was hurt. He's still worth drafting as a No. 2 Fantasy running back, but don't reach for Love before Round 4.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Javonte Williams (ADP of 35.1), D'Andre Swift (ADP of 38.1) and Travis Etienne (ADP of 39.6)Cam SkatteboI expect Skattebo to be the best running back for the Giants, and I don't mind drafting him as a No. 2 Fantasy option. But his CBS Sports ADP is too high at 34.8, and the earliest I would draft him is Round 5. We don't know exactly how the depth chart will look in New York, but Skattebo is expected to share touches with some combination of Tyrone Tracy Jr., Devin Singletary and Najee Harris. Tracy might be falling out of favor after some pass protection concerns and a lost fumble in the preseason, but Skattebo could still come off the field in crucial situations. That wasn't the case during his rookie campaign in 2025 when he scored at least 13 PPR points in six games in a row from Weeks 2-7 before suffering a season-ending broken ankle in Week 8. He averaged 19.1 PPR points over that span, including four outings with at least 19 total touches. We'll see what happens as the season goes on, but Skattebo in a potential committee should not be drafted in Round 3.
(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Javonte Williams (ADP of 35.1), D'Andre Swift (ADP of 38.1) and Travis Etienne (ADP of 39.6)TreVeyon HendersonI'm still hopeful for Henderson to be a star in his sophomore campaign, but I would not draft him at his current CBS Sports ADP at 65.4. I view Henderson as more of a high-end flex, and the earliest I would draft him is No. 75 overall. Henderson showed plenty of potential in a few games last season, especially in Weeks 9-11 when Rhamondre Stevenson was injured, and Henderson averaged 24.3 PPR points over that span. He also scored 30.1 PPR points in Week 15 against Buffalo and 17.3 PPR points in Week 18 against Miami. But if you remove those five games then Henderson averaged just 6.4 PPR points in his other 16 outings, including the playoffs. For the year, he appeared in 18 games with Stevenson, who played more snaps than Henderson in 15 of those contests. It would be great to see Henderson take a step forward this season and keep Stevenson on the bench, but that's hard to expect given what happened in 2025 and all the reports this preseason. Henderson might only be a Fantasy starter if Stevenson were to miss any time due to injury.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Rhamondre Stevenson (ADP of 79.8) and Jonathon Brooks (ADP of 87.9)
Mike EvansSince training camp started, Evans has already missed practice time due to quadriceps, foot and ankle injuries. None of them are considered serious, but it's not a great sign for Evans, who turned 33 this week. As a reminder, he missed 12 games over the past two seasons due to hamstring and collarbone injuries, and we don't want to draft a receiver in Round 5 who could struggle to stay on the field. That said, I do expect him to be a solid contributor for the 49ers, and another season of at least 1,000 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns is possible in this offense. But it's now a crowded receiving corps with George Kittle (Achilles) healthy, Deebo Samuel back and the emergence of rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, who is having a strong preseason. And let's not forget about McCaffrey when healthy. Evans has top-20 upside, but the earliest I would draft him is Round 6 in all leagues.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Rome Odunze (ADP of 66.4), Christian Watson (ADP of 72.6) and Parker Washington (ADP of 82.7) Courtland SuttonI don't mind drafting Sutton as a potential No. 3 Fantasy receiver in all leagues, but I don't love his CBS Sports ADP at 80.7. That makes him WR32, which is too soon, and he's WR39 in my rankings. You know the deal by now with Sutton following the addition of Jaylen Waddle, and Pat Bryant earned positive reviews in training camp. Sutton will lose targets, and he averaged 129.5 targets over the past two seasons. Now, he could still be a viable threat for Bo Nix, especially in the end zone, and he has averaged 7.5 touchdowns over the past two years. But there are receivers who have more upside being drafted after Sutton, and I would rather draft him as a high-end reserve in three-receiver leagues as opposed to a must-start option. The earliest I would draft Sutton is Round 8.
(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Parker Washington (ADP of 82.7), Brian Thomas Jr. (84.6) and Chris Godwin (94.4)Alec PiercePierce initially underwent a clean-up procedure on his left ankle in April, and he was facing a three-month recovery timetable. He started training camp on the active/PUP list, where he remains as of Monday. There's no way you should draft him at his CBS Sports ADP of 84.3 this close to the season, and the earliest I would draft him is Round 11. Josh Downs is the better Colts receiver to draft, and it's now close between Pierce and Keenan Allen, who was signed last week due to Pierce remaining out. Pierce closed last year on a tear, scoring at least 13 PPR points in four of his final six outings, but that was when Daniel Jones (Achilles) was out. In nine games with Jones to start the season, Pierce averaged just 10.2 PPR points per game. He could still be a difference maker as the season goes on once he's healthy, but don't reach for Pierce on Draft Day. He's not someone I would draft before Round 10.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Brian Thomas Jr. (84.6), Chris Godwin (94.4) and Josh Downs (ADP of 115.9)DK MetcalfIt feels like Fantasy managers are still drafting Metcalf based on his name and not his game. At least the way he played the game in 2025. In his first year with the Steelers, Metcalf had career lows in targets (99) and yards (850), and his 59 receptions was the second-lowest mark of his career. He also scored just six touchdowns, and this is four years in a row with him finding the end zone in single digits. Metcalf and Aaron Rodgers are not a good match since Rodgers doesn't want to consistently challenge downfield at this point in his career. Metcalf now has to share the field with Michael Pittman, and Pittsburgh added rookie Germie Bernard in the second round of the NFL Draft. Metcalf's CBS Sports ADP is WR37 at 90.6, which isn't bad, but I don't want to draft him as a starter even in three-receiver leagues. I have Metcalf ranked as WR43 at No. 99 overall, and I'm close to ranking him behind Pittman, who should be a better fit for Rodgers. This should be another frustrating season for Metcalf and his Fantasy production.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: Chris Godwin (ADP of 94.4), Quentin Johnston (ADP of 103.6) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ADP of 107.6)Harold Fannin Jr.Fannin was amazing in 2025 as a rookie, and he closed the year on a tear with at least 11 PPR points in five games in a row, while averaging 15.8 PPR points over that span. It helped propel Fannin to the No. 8 PPR tight end for the season, and he finished the year with 72 catches for 731 yards and six touchdowns on 107 targets, which led the team. But three significant factors have changed for Fannin heading into this year. For starters, Kevin Stefanski is gone as the head coach, and he has been fantastic for tight ends in his career. New coach Todd Monken also likes to involve his tight ends, but it's not the same level as Stefanski. Along with that, there's more competition for targets this season after Cleveland drafted KC Concepcion with the No. 24 overall pick in the first round of the NFL Draft and Denzel Boston in Round 2 at No. 39 overall. Jerry Jeudy remains on the roster, and Fannin isn't guaranteed to lead the team in targets again. Finally, we have a quarterback change with Deshaun Watson -- who hasn't played football since Week 7 in 2024 due to an Achilles injury -- starting in place of Shedeur Sanders. Watson doesn't have a great history throwing to tight ends, and Sanders helped Fannin break out at the end of 2025. I would still draft Fannin as a No. 1 Fantasy tight end this season, but I don't like his CBS Sports ADP at 83.6. The earliest I would draft Fannin is Round 8.(BOLD) I'd rather draft: George Kittle (ADP of 92.4) and Isaiah Likely (ADP of 97.8)

title: Florida names Aaron Philo starting QB: Georgia Tech transfer tapped to lead Gators in 2026 - CBS Sports
description: What to know about the first-year starter and who he beat during fall camp
body:
What to know about the first-year starter and who he beat during fall camp
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Coming out of Florida's second fall scrimmage, Gators coach Jon Sumrall named Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo as the team's starting quarterback ahead of next month's opener against FAU.  One of Florida's top transfers this cycle after joining former Yellow Jackets offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner in Gainesville, Philo backed up Haynes King last season and beat out Tramell Jones Jr. for the job with the Gators.Philo has received most of the first-team reps during the last week of practice and reportedly impressed during Saturday night's scrimmage, highlighted by a 15-yard touchdown run early on.Undecided on Florida's quarterback battle after spring, Sumrall said the position remained even earlier this month as both players pushed for the job. That changed after Sumrall and his offensive staff reviewed film over the weekend.He said Monday that Philo will get the "lion's share of reps" this week as game prep begins.
"We are preparing for him to be the starter for Week 1," Sumrall said.Sumrall's still a believer in Tramell JonesSumrall stressed that Philo is the starter for the first game."There will not be some crazy hoopla around it in our building, it's just how we're moving forward," Sumrall said Monday. "I met with both guys and both are awesome. I'm excited about the room. The good news is both of them have elevated their play. Love both of them and I'm fired up for both of them."It's been a real battle, it's not been some empty competition. It's been real and that's where we are."From pre-snap checks to reading defenses and being able to "kill" bad calls, Philo showed superiority.
"He has operated at the line of scrimmage at a touch higher level," Sumrall said. "There's no surprise in the spring because he'd been in the system and Tramell had not. We're able to operate the full offense at a little bit higher level with Aaron, with the whole level. Their arm talent is very similar. What's unique is both of them's play style resembles each other more than it differentiates."Sumrall also said that Philo has seen the "middle of the field" a bit more during practice."I talked to Aaron this is not an anointing," Sumrall said. "(This) is not some permanent, you're the starter forever. For Tramell, it's not like you're being relegated or demoted and forgotten. This is not fatal. I'm a believer in Tramell Jones. I just feel like right now it's where we need to go with the decision, but the guys will rally around both."
Faulkner's offensive scheme at FloridaFaulkner wants a passer who can operate quickly, distribute the football in space and punish defenses when safeties creep toward the line of scrimmage. Philo checks every box. He played with confidence at Georgia Tech, understanding leverage and has enough mobility to extend possessions without abandoning the structure of the offense. Those are two areas of strength Philo reportedly displayed during both camp scrimmages this month.Most importantly, Philo's comfortable playing aggressively. Florida needs a quarterback capable of creating explosive plays while keeping the offense on schedule, and Philo's experience in Faulkner's system should accelerate that transition. 
There will be adjustments against SEC defenses, but the scheme familiarity makes Philo a natural fit for what Florida wants offensively.

title: NWSL TOTW: Mallory Swanson shines for Chicago Stars FC, Portland Thorns honor Tobin Heath - CBS Sports
description: The Attacking Third crew picked their best XI from the past week's NWSL action
body:
The Attacking Third crew picked their best XI from the past week's NWSL action
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET
                        
                •

        As the calendar enters the final third of the schedule for the 2026 NWSL regular season, it's no surprise players are still producing big moments. Whether it's on the pitch or off, it's time to roll out Attacking Third's NWSL Team of the Week honors.Everyone's favorite content trend is back for another season. After weekly matches across the 2026 NWSL season, Attacking Third analysts will select a team of the week, head coach, and honorary captain based on performances across the weekend.Here you can find a mix of stats and data, analysis from our pundits, and highlights you may have missed over the weekend. If you're keeping track of who earned past honors, check out our previous team of the week.This week, we had a bit more fun, even changed up our preferred lineup formation, and saluted an NWSL legend. Coaches made history too, so congratulations to Karina Baez on becoming the first-ever Mexican woman to earn a regular-season win in a head coaching role. 
Here's who made the latest edition:
Goalkeeper: Jordan Silkowitz (Bay FC)Jordan Silkowitz has put her goalkeeper skills on display all year for Bay FC. Her 85 saves through 19 games this season lead the entire league, and while it's a stat that can sometimes say more about the team's entire defensive state, it's still impressive. This week she's on the team for another shot-stopping clinic against Houston Dash.
Defender: Rafaelle (Orlando Pride)Orlando have to scrap their way out of a slump, and that oftentimes starts out back. Pride defender and Brazilian international Rafaelle was non-stop in providing defensive coverage against Washington Spirit. She led the team in shot blocks (three) and clearances (18).Defender: Jayden Perry (Portland Thorns FC)Sometimes the defensive play that helps the most is the ones that come when you're capable of controlling the ball and aiding in distribution and that's what Thorns FC fullback Jayden Perry did over the weekend. She helped Portland pick up their first clean sheet since July 5. 
Defender: Sarah Gorden (Angel City)Angel City defender Sarah Gorden is a league veteran and knows how to produce big moments when the team needs it. She picked up two critical blocks against Gotham FC to disrupt any link-ups between Sam Kerr and Jaedyn Shaw.
Midfielder: Lauren Milliet (Racing Louisville) A double match week for Louisville and Lauren Milliet's three assists over two games put her into the team as we tweak our lineup a bit. She delivered a heads-up assist off a short throw-in.
Midfielder: Jessie Fleming (Portland Thorns)Portland Thorns midfielder Jessie Fleming showed off her vision and line-breaking pass ability with this long ball through to find Sophia Wilson for a goal.
Midfielder: Haley McCutcheon (Orlando Pride)Barbra Banda is back, and Pride midfielder Haley McCutcheon welcomed her back by getting a foot on this great pass for the game winner against Washington Spirit.
Midfielder: Mallory Swanson (Chicago Stars FC)Welcome back to the team, Mallory Swanson. This week it's for her skillful spin-in-the-box goal and an epic call-your-shot assist to Jameese Joseph. 
Forward: Ashley Sanchez (North Carolina Courage)There's a new leader in the NWSL Golden Boot race, and it's North Carolina Courage winger Ashley Sanchez. She doesn't look like she'll stop scoring anytime soon. 
Forward: Trinity Byars (San Diego Wave FC)San Diego have been on the hunt for goals several weeks now, and thankfully, Trinity Byars is the answer. Two goals and an assist for team of the week honors, and what a sprint for this go-ahead goal.
Forward: Kat Rader (Houston Dash)Midweek games can feel like forever ago, but they still count for team of the week memories. Rookie Kat Rader is having a good season for the Dash and can't stop scoring. 
Coach: Karina Baez (Chicago Stars FC)After a head coaching change, a shift in staff, and one draw later, the Chicago Stars finally got a win for interim head coach Karina Baez. A 3-2 win over Racing Louisville, which ended their four-game win streak, finally brought some joy to the lakefront for Chicago. A historic one too: Karina Baez becomes the first-ever Mexican woman to win an NWSL game in a head coaching role. 
Honorary captain: Tobin Heath (Portland Thorns)For a brief moment, all was right in the NWSL universe because Tobin Heath was able to sign a one-day contract and officially retire as a Portland Thorns player. The U.S. Soccer Hall of Famer, two-time World Cup winner, Olympic gold medalist, and all-around certified baller was just as decorated in league play. She's the club's all-time assist leader (66) and won two NWSL Championships (2013, 2017) and the NWSL Shield (2016). She held the all-time single-season assist record (10) for nearly a decade before Croix Bethune matched the 10 assists in 2024. Her number is now retired in Portland, but her legacy is forever.
